pages.name: Spiderling
pages.text: Tame it, and it follows you everywhere.

$(item)Taming$()$(br)Offer meat to a wild spiderling. Not every try works. A tamed spiderling follows you, fights for you, and sits when told to.$(br2)Wild ones hunt sheep, rabbits, foxes, baby turtles and skeletons, and flee llamas.

$(item)Climber$()$(br)It climbs walls, shrugs off cobwebs and takes no harm from falls. It slowly mends on its own.$(br2)Once it has grown big enough, it will carry a rider, and a rider can make it leap.

$(item)Traits$()$(br)Size, health, speed and leaping strength differ from one spiderling to the next.$(br2)Two tamed spiderlings in the mood have a child near the average of their traits, give or take some chance. Choose your parents well.
$(item)Feeding$()$(br)Meat mends a spiderling. Locust snacks mend it far better and put a rested, tamed, adult pair in the mood. A golden locust snack mends the most and grows a young one fastest.
$(item)Potion effects$()$(br)A spiderling treats potions differently. Every helpful or neutral effect it receives lasts forever, at the same strength.$(br2)Harmful effects wear off as usual.
$(item)Washing$()$(br)Washing a spiderling strips every effect off it at once, good or bad, with the hiss of a doused fire.$(br2)Choose its potions carefully before you make them permanent.
